newsitem.title: EGYPT: Kuwait expects U.S. to share deployment costs.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait expects U.S. to share deployment costs.

text.p: The Kuwaiti foreign minister said in an interview published on Wednesday he thought Kuwait and the United States, and possibly other Gulf states, would share the costs of the U.S. troop deployment in the Gulf.

"This subject will be discussed later and I believe that Kuwait will not bear the burden alone. There will be a Kuwaiti contribution, as well as an American contribution," the minister, Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Jaber al-Sabah, told the London-based newspaper al-Hayat in an interview conducted in London.
The United States and its allies charged Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and other Gulf states for much of the costs of the war to drive Iraqi troops out of Kuwait in 1991.
But Saudi Arabia has not been enthusiastic about this month's U.S. deployment, which responded to Iraqi military action inside Iraqi territory in the Kurdish north.

This time the United States has fired 44 cruise missiles, diverted an aircraft carrier from the Adriatic to the Gulf and sent eight F-117A Stealth bombers to Kuwait. About 3,500 U.S. troops are preparing to fly to the Gulf.
Asked if other Gulf states would contribute money this time, Sheikh Sabah said: "This subject will be discussed later. I will not anticipate events."

Asked about differences between Gulf states over the tension in the Gulf, he only said that a meeting of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) had issued a statement. But the statement did not mention the U.S. attacks on Iraqi targets.
Sheikh Sabah denied that in Cairo last week he had said no troops would cross into Iraq territory from Kuwait.
"If a threat to Kuwait arose, I could not prevent anyone from crossing the border to protect my land and my people," he added.

The minister said he could not predict whether the United States would strike Iraq again. "All we hope is that this (Iraqi) regime will come to an end from inside Iraq and not from outside, so that the Iraqi people can live a dignified life with the Arab family," he added.
